html:
SMTO-WEB-0028 — This result hasn't been shown to meet all your requirements

GUID: 65a20faa-27e1-5cdd-a1f0-673c1f97bb6e
Slug: research-hard-constraint-not-verified
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • An item in the answer hasn't been proven to match every must-have requirement in your request, such as a location, price or model. SMTO won't list it as a match.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the run to finish. SMTO sends the answer back to the Model and asks it to keep only results that meet every requirement or check the missing one. The check found an item listed as a match before all your must-haves were confirmed.
  2. If the run stops, ask SMTO to confirm the missing requirement for that item, or to report only the results it could confirm. A partial answer that says what is still unconfirmed is allowed; an unproven match is not.
  3. If a requirement can be loosened, say so plainly in a new message, for example "ships from the EU is fine". SMTO won't relax a requirement on its own, and treats a similar detail as different unless you say so.

What success looks like

  • The answer lists only items that meet every requirement, or clearly says which ones couldn't be confirmed.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't accept a substitute check in place of what you asked for, such as where an item is located instead of where the seller is based.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof rejected a definite claim about a subject outside eligible_results (hard constraints not verified), or an UNCERTAIN claim while the research contract disallows unverified results.

What this means

  • A definite claim uses a subject outside eligible_results, or an uncertain claim is submitted when the contract disallows unverified results. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • A definite claim uses a subject outside eligible_results, or an uncertain claim is submitted when the contract disallows unverified results.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect excluded-result reasons and allow_unverified_results rather than assuming a failed real-world property.

How to fix it

  • Raised as research_hard_constraint_not_verified in _validate_answer; the rejection details include the subject's exclusion reasons. Drop unqualified subjects, verify the missing constraint predicates from EVIDENCE sources, or return status partial with a scoped limitation; do not relax a hard constraint or substitute a proxy predicate (for example item location for seller country).
  • Remove unqualified matches, verify the missing constraints through authorized evidence, or report a supported partial result.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • Only verified eligible results are stated as matches; permitted partial limitations remain explicit.

What not to do

  • Do not relax a required filter without authorization or substitute item location for seller country.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
